entities.summary:
Bardas Parsakoutenos was a Byzantine public servant who played a crucial role in the governance of the Eastern Roman Empire during the 9th century.

As a military leader, Bardas Parsakoutenos was part of the imperial guard and held the rank of magistros, a high-ranking position that indicated his significance within the imperial administration.


Bardas Parsakoutenos's most notable achievement was his participation in the 901 CE rebellion against Emperor Leo VI.


The rebellion led by Bardas Parsakoutenos was ultimately unsuccessful, but it marked a turning point in the struggle for power within the imperial court.


Despite his failure, Bardas Parsakoutenos left a lasting legacy in the annals of Byzantine history, demonstrating the complexities and intrigue of the imperial system.


One of the most striking aspects of Bardas Parsakoutenos's story is the way it highlights the tensions between the imperial court and the military, a conflict that would shape the course of Byzantine history for centuries to come.
